title: Group and phase velocity in WR-90 waveguide
caption: The TE₁₀ cut-off of WR-90 (a = 2.29 cm) is f_c = c/2a = 6.6 GHz. Above it v_g = c√(1 − (f_c/f)²) rises from zero while v_p = c/√(1 − (f_c/f)²) falls from infinity; at 10 GHz, inside X-band, v_g = 0.76c and v_p = 1.32c. The product v_g v_p = c² always, so the phase velocity exceeds c while the signal travels slower than c.
alt: Graph of velocity relative to c against frequency from 6.5 to 12 gigahertz: the group velocity rising from zero at 6.6 GHz towards 1, and the phase velocity falling from a large value towards 1, with the X-band range 8 to 12 GHz shaded.
description: The horizontal axis is frequency in gigahertz; the vertical axis is velocity in units of c.
The group velocity starts at zero at cut-off and rises towards c; at 10 GHz it is 0.76c.
The phase velocity starts very large at cut-off and falls towards c; at 10 GHz it is 1.32c. The two multiply to c².
